questions.q: The "Chairman" of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by:
questions.e: The Speaker appoints the chairman from among the committee members. Since 1967, the chairman has been selected from the Opposition.

questions.q: Which of the following "Audit Reports" of the CAG are examined by the PAC? 1️⃣ Audit report on appropriation accounts. 2️⃣ Audit report on finance accounts. 3️⃣ Audit report on public undertakings.
questions.e: The PAC examines all three annual audit reports submitted by the CAG to the President.

questions.q: The "Membership" of the Estimates Committee was raised from 25 to 30 in which year?
questions.e: Originally consisting of 25 members in 1950, the membership of the Estimates Committee was increased to 30 in 1956.

questions.q: Why is the "Estimates Committee" described as a "Continuous Economy Committee"?
o: Because it suggests administrative reforms to reduce spending
Because it is headed by the Finance Minister
Because its term is for five years
questions.e: It suggests economies, improvements in organization, and efficiency consistent with the policy underlying the estimates.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding "Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs": 1️⃣ It consists of 30 members. 2️⃣ 20 members are from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha. 3️⃣ It considers reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs.
questions.e: This committee has 30 members (20 LS, 10 RS) and is tasked with examining matters relating to safeguards and welfare programs for SCs and STs.

questions.q: Which committee examines whether the "Executive" is properly exercising the powers to make regulations and bye-laws delegated by Parliament?
questions.e: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines and reports if delegated legislation is being properly used.

questions.q: The "Railway Convention Committee" is an example of:
questions.e: It is an ad hoc committee constituted from time to time to determine dividends payable by Railways.

questions.q: "Consultative Committees" are constituted by the:
questions.e: These informal bodies for discussion between ministers and MPs are set up by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

questions.q: The "Indian Parliamentary Group" Newsletter is brought out every:
questions.e: An uninterrupted flow of info is maintained via the IPG Newsletter, which is published quarterly.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio "President" of the Indian Parliamentary Group?
questions.e: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha serves as the ex-officio President of the IPG.

questions.q: "Associate Members" of the IPG are NOT entitled to which of the following? 1️⃣ Representation at conferences of the IPU and CPA. 2️⃣ Travel concessions provided by CPA branches. 3️⃣ Receiving the IPG Newsletter.
questions.e: Associate members (former MPs) have limited rights; they cannot represent the group at conferences or use CPA travel concessions. They *do* receive the newsletter.

questions.q: The "Supreme Court of India" replaced which body as the highest court of appeal in 1950?
questions.e: While the SC succeeded the Federal Court, it also replaced the British Privy Council as the final appellate body.

questions.q: The "sanctioned strength" of the Supreme Court was increased to 34 (including the CJI) in which year?
questions.e: Through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, the number was raised to 33 other judges plus the CJI.

questions.q: What is the "obligatory" consultation for the President when appointing a Supreme Court judge?
o: Consultation with the Chief Justice of India
Consultation with the entire Collegium of 9 judges
questions.e: Article 124 states that consultation with the CJI is mandatory for the appointment of any judge other than the CJI.

questions.q: In the "First Judges Case" (1981), the court held that:
o: The President has no role in appointments
Consultation only implies exchange of views
questions.e: Initially, the court held that consultation did not mean concurrence, allowing the executive more discretion.

questions.q: The "99th Amendment Act" and "NJAC Act" were declared unconstitutional in which case?
questions.e: In the Fourth Judges Case (2015), the SC struck down the NJAC as it would affect judicial independence.

questions.q: Which of the following is a "Qualification" for an SC judge?
o: Practicing lawyer in the Supreme Court for 20 years
Judge of a High Court for at least 5 years
Member of the Rajya Sabha for 10 years
questions.e: Qualification includes being a HC judge for 5 years or a HC advocate for 10 years.

questions.q: A "Pensions" of Supreme Court judges are:
o: Subject to the annual vote of Parliament
Paid by the respective High Courts
Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
questions.e: All salaries and pensions of SC judges are "charged" expenditure, meaning they are non-votable to protect independence.

questions.q: "Ad hoc Judges" can be appointed by the CJI only with:
o: The previous consent of the President
The approval of the Lok Sabha
The consent of the Prime Minister
The recommendation of the Law Ministry
questions.e: Under Article 127, the CJI needs the President's previous consent and must consult the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.

questions.q: "Exclusive Original Jurisdiction" of the SC excludes which of the following?
o: Disputes where Center and one state are against others
Disputes between the Centre and States
Disputes arising out of pre-constitution treaties
Disputes between two or more states
questions.e: Disputes from treaties signed before the Constitution's commencement are specifically excluded from Article 131.

questions.q: The SC can issue writs for the enforcement of "Fundamental Rights" under which Article?
questions.e: Article 32 empowers the SC to issue writs (habeas corpus, etc.) for protecting fundamental rights.

questions.q: "Special Leave to Appeal" (Article 136) is:
o: A discretionary power of the Supreme Court
A matter of right for every citizen
questions.e: The SC has the discretion to grant special leave to appeal against any judgment from any court/tribunal (except military).

questions.q: Under Article 143, the SC "must" tender its opinion to the President in which case?
o: On disputes between two private citizens
On matters regarding the appointment of ministers
On any question of law of public importance
On any dispute arising out of a pre-constitution treaty
questions.e: The SC *may* refuse an opinion on general legal questions but *must* provide one on pre-constitution treaty disputes.

questions.q: The "Power to punish for contempt" of the Supreme Court extends to: 1️⃣ Itself. 2️⃣ High Courts. 3️⃣ Subordinate Courts.
questions.e: In 1991, the SC ruled it can punish for contempt of itself and all lower courts/tribunals nationwide.

questions.q: "Judicial Review" categorized by Justice Syed Shah Mohamed Quadri includes review of:
o: Constitutional amendments, legislation, and administrative actions
questions.e: Quadri's classification covers the full spectrum of state actions.

questions.q: Which case established the "Basic Structure" doctrine?
questions.e: The 1973 Kesavananda Bharati case ruled that Parliament cannot amend the "basic features" of the Constitution.

questions.q: "Judicial Review" in India is a synthesis of:
o: American judicial supremacy and British parliamentary supremacy
questions.e: India recognizes both the US principle of supremacy and the UK principle of parliamentary power, but with significant limitations on both.

questions.q: Laws in the Ninth Schedule are tested on the touchstone of:
questions.e: Since the I.R. Coelho case, 9th Schedule laws must be tested against the "golden triangle" of Articles 14, 19, and 21.

questions.q: "Judicial Activism" is often practiced in India through:
questions.e: PIL is the most popular manifestation of judicial activism in the Indian system.

questions.q: "Judicial Restraint" assumptions include:
o: The Court has absolute expertise in economic matters
The Court is the most democratic branch
The Court should run the government
The Court should defer to democratic branches wherever possible
questions.e: Restraint assumes that since the Court is non-elective, it should respect the "more" democratic branches (legislature/executive).

questions.q: Who among the following laid the foundations of "Judicial Activism" in India?
o: Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer and Justice P.N. Bhagwati
questions.e: Justices Iyer, Bhagwati, Reddy, and Desai were the pioneers in the mid-1970s.

questions.q: The "Golden Triangle" of fundamental rights includes:
questions.e: These three articles are central to the "rights test" applied to evaluate the validity of 9th Schedule laws.

questions.q: "PIL" is absolutely necessary for: 1️⃣ Maintaining the rule of law. 2️⃣ Furthering the cause of justice. 3️⃣ Accelerating the pace of constitutional objectives.
questions.e: PIL serves these three primary purposes in the Indian legal landscape.

questions.q: The Supreme Court modified "PIL guidelines" in which year?
questions.e: Guidelines were first formulated in 1988 and modified in 1993 and 2003.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a ground for challenging an enactment via "Judicial Review"?
o: Outside the competence of the authority
The law is "unwise" in the opinion of the court
questions.e: In India, courts examine *substantive* validity (power/competence) rather than the "wisdom" or policy implications of a law.

questions.q: "Locus Standi" relaxation means:
o: The President must approve every case
Any member of the public with "sufficient interest" can approach the court
Only a lawyer can file a case
The court can only hear cases from Delhi
questions.e: It allows public-spirited individuals to seek redress for those unable to do so due to poverty or ignorance.

questions.q: The "Surya Narain case" (1981) dealt with:
o: The term and removal of the Governor
questions.e: The Supreme Court held that the President's pleasure in removing a Governor is not justifiable.

questions.q: A Governor can "resign" by addressing a letter to:
questions.e: Article 156(2) states the Governor may resign by writing to the President.

questions.q: "Personal Immunity" of the Governor includes: 1️⃣ Immunity from criminal proceedings during term of office. 2️⃣ Immunity from arrest or imprisonment. 3️⃣ Immunity from civil proceedings regarding official acts.
questions.e: Governors enjoy full immunity from criminal cases and arrest while in office. They also have personal immunity for their official acts.

questions.q: The "State Election Commissioner" can be removed:
o: By the Governor at any time
By the State Legislature by a simple majority
Only in the same manner as a judge of a High Court
questions.e: While the Governor appoints him, the SEC has security of tenure similar to a High Court judge.

questions.q: Which "Amendment Act" added Article 124A regarding the NJAC?
questions.e: The 99th Amendment sought to create the NJAC to reform judge appointments.

questions.q: "Judicial Activism" activators focusing on forestry and the Fifth/Sixth Schedules are:
questions.e: Baxi identified indigenous groups as those agitating for forest dwellers and schedule-based identity rights.

questions.q: "Statutory Resolutions" are those moved:
o: Either by a Private Member or a Minister in pursuance of a law
questions.e: These are resolutions moved based on a provision in the Constitution or an Act of Parliament.

questions.q: "Half-an-Hour Discussion" can be allotted by the Speaker:
questions.e: This device is for matters of public importance needing factual elucidation; the Speaker can allot three days a week for it.

questions.q: The "Kihoto Hollohan case" (1992) established that the Speaker's decision on defection is:
o: Subject to approval by the PM
questions.e: The SC ruled that the Speaker acts as a tribunal under the 10th Schedule, and thus his decisions are subject to court review.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the "High Court" to issue writs?
questions.e: Article 226 allows High Courts to issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and other legal purposes.

questions.q: The "Rules Committee" of Lok Sabha consists of:
questions.e: The Lok Sabha Rules Committee has 15 members, including the Speaker as ex-officio chairman.

questions.q: "Youth Parliament" objectives include:
o: Training students to become IAS officers
Acquainting younger generations with practices of Parliament
Providing scholarships to political science students
questions.e: It aims to acquaint youth with procedures and inculcate democratic values.

questions.q: Who described the "Leader of Opposition" as the "alternative Prime Minister"?
questions.e: Ivor Jennings used this description to highlight the role of the shadow cabinet and the opposition's readiness to form a government.
